analysis:
The CHANGELOG.md units (7e16eb3337db8652:12 and :13) are documentation only and have no security impact. In coordinator/api/install.sh, the PR adds bind_provider_coordinator and provider_websocket_url. The installer now binds provider.toml to the coordinator that served it. For production (https://api.darkbloom.dev) it removes any [coordinator] url so the provider uses its built-in default. For any other coordinator it writes a wss:// URL, or ws:// only for localhost or 127.0.0.1. TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider WebSocket) is the relevant boundary, and the change does not weaken it.

Injection: the host is validated against ^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?$, so a crafted COORD_URL cannot inject TOML. Paths, userinfo and whitespace are rejected.

Downgrade: plaintext ws is restricted to loopback hosts, so a non-local coordinator cannot be set over an unencrypted link.

Redirection: COORD_URL comes from the coordinator-served installer or the operator's own environment. The adversary here (ADV-001) is the Mac owner and is not gaining new capability. Removing the url also moves a previously dev-bound config back to production, which is the safer direction.

File handling: the config is written through a tmp file and mv in the user's own config directory. The original file mode may be reset to the umask default. I rated this negligible because provider.toml holds no secrets according to the supplied context.

Limits: dotted-key or inline-table forms of the coordinator URL are not handled by the awk script, so a pre-existing url in that form would persist. That is a robustness gap and not a security regression. If the installer's placeholder is left unreplaced or the URL is malformed, the script exits 1 after the binaries are installed. This is an availability and robustness concern only.

The --bind-coordinator-test hook is local and unprivileged. Because the changes touch only the installer and docs, I found no cross-file interactions with attestation, billing or encryption. I did not review the provider's ProviderConfig.swift consumption of the url, which is outside the supplied units.
